summary: Gives IANA directions for managing a registry of special-purpose IPv6 address assignments. This memo is informational. It was replaced by RFC 6890.

eli5.summary: Some IPv6 addresses are set aside for special jobs. This note tells the address-keepers how to keep the list of who got what. It was later replaced.

questions: iana special purpose ipv6 address registry
who manages special ipv6 address blocks
what is the iana special purpose ipv6 registry
subtitle: A direction to IANA to keep a registry of special-purpose IPv6 address blocks, later replaced by RFC 6890.

tldr.problem: IANA held a block of IPv6 space for testing and experiments, and needed direction on registering special-purpose designations from it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC directs IANA to open a Special Purpose IPv6 address registry that records each designation's prefix, the RFC that called for it, dates, purpose, contact and routing scope.
tldr.outcome: This RFC was obsoleted by RFC 6890, which is the current reference.

today: RFC 4773 has been obsoleted by RFC 6890, which replaces it.

sections.title: Background
sections.content:
RFC 4773 is a direction to IANA on managing the IANA Special Purpose IPv6 address assignment registry. RFC 2928 assigned a block of Sub-TLA IDs to IANA for testing and experimental use, such as the 6bone and new approaches like exchanges. RFC 2860 treats specialised address blocks and experimental assignments as part of IANA's technical work.

The RFC directs IANA to designate special purpose blocks under the criteria of RFC 2928 and to open a registry for them. Entries cover experimental addresses and other special cases documented in IESG-reviewed RFCs.
sections.eli5: A chunk of addresses was set aside for experiments. This note says to start a proper list of what each piece is for.

sections.title: The Registry and Its Rules
sections.content:
The pool is 2001:0000::/23, assigned to IANA in July 1999 by RFC 2928. Further space may be added to it only through an IETF Consensus action, consistent with prevailing IANA IPv6 policies. IANA may designate addresses when an IESG-reviewed RFC requests them for IETF testing or experiments, or for specialised use such as anycast with a Standards Track protocol.

For each designation the registry records the prefix, the calling RFC, the date, any end date, the purpose, the responsible entity for experimental unicast uses, and the intended routing scope. Listed prefixes are not guaranteed routability. IANA will not keep sub-registries for these blocks.
sections.eli5: For every special piece, the list says who has it, why, when, and how far it may travel.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Routing security relies on authenticating an assertion of unique control of an address block. The registry is meant to be an authoritative source on the currency and purpose of special use blocks, a small step toward a framework that could serve as a trust point for chains of address validation. The RFC suggests machine-parseable publication formats and file signatures with associated certificates.
sections.eli5: A trusted list helps everyone check that a claim to an address is real.
